ENTHUSIASM MARKS SOUTHWESTERN MEETING
CONTINUES FIGHT FOR MANY MORE IMPROVEMENTS
Icy And Wet Weather Was Not Enough To Dampen Enthusiasm Of Civic Workers

Scores of improvement measures for the Brooklyn community underwent a thorough discussion at the first 1924 meeting of the Southwestern Civic and Business Men's association, held last Monday evening, in the association's hall, 4154 Pearl rd. The streets were icy and so were the sidewalks and it was wet both above and under foot, but all this did not keep a good, enthusiastic crowd from attending the meeting, the first to be presided over by the newly-elected president, Ira D. Siegfried. The association at the meeting instructed its secretary to ask the proper city authorities to act to relieve the insanitary conditions caused by lack of proper sewer system in the area between State and Ridge rd. and between Shiller ave. and Brookpark rd. Mr. E. T. Buhl reported that his committee had been studying means for getting electric lights for illumination of Parma's main highways. J. P. Smith reported on the progress of the committee selected to obtain a house numbering system for Parma Township. E. C. Brandes called attention to the dangerous traffic condition on State road, near Cypress. Unification of city and county under one government and elimination of various industries that emitted offensive odors, was proposed by Senator L. G. Collister.

ACT TO IMPROVE RURAL MAIL SERVICE
Plan To Bring City Delivery For Residents In North Section Of Parma Township

Interested in bringing about better mail service throughout the entire Brooklyn community, President Ira D. Siegfried, of the Southwestern Civic and Business Men's Association, has selected a committee to take up the matter with the postal authorities. The committee already has started to work and has made interesting progress. To get city delivery for most of Parma Township between Pearl and State roads, north of Snow road, is the aim of the association, and according to the superintendent of the Brooklyn post office station, such a step would eliminate much of the mail irregularity on the rural route on State road. However, before city delivery can be furnished, the streets must be supplied with sidewalks and the houses must be numbered.

DOINGS OF VARIOUS MOTHERS CLUBS
An Ideal Completely Organized

Parent-Teachers' associations or mothers' clubs are now established throughout the entire Brooklyn district, including Brooklyn Heights and Parma. Mrs. H. J. Coates, of Memphis Association; Mrs. H. H. Waite, of Dawning Association; Mrs. H. H. Beebe, of Lady of Good Counsel; Mrs. J. W. Speed, of Benjamin Franklin; Mrs. Carl Haag, of Pearl road; Mrs. Homer Apel, of Ridge Road; Mrs. Arthur Brown, State Road; Mrs. Paul F. Hasse, Brooklyn Heights; Mrs. Horace Gemeiner, of Broadview School.

PLAN MASQUERADE

The Broadview Parent-Teachers' Association held a dance Saturday evening, January 26th, which was well attended. Plans are now being made for a prize masquerade which will be held Saturday evening, Feb. 9th, at Broadview school. Gimbel's orchestra will play. Prizes for best and comic costumes.

AT BEN FRANKLIN SCHOOL

An interesting meeting of the Ben Franklin Parent-Teachers' Association was held at the school last Wednesday evening. Miss Bessie Dalton, principal, was one of the speakers and an address on the subject of "Korea" was delivered by S. F. Brockman of the International Committee of the Y. M. C. A. The new school orchestra, directed by Mrs. Philip Klem, furnished music. The next meeting will be held February 20.

Parma Parent-Teachers

Parma-Ridgewood Parent-Teachers will meet Tuesday, Feb. 6th. Mrs. Elsie Cleverdon, of the County Board of Education, will speak at this meeting. All members are urged to be present.

DENISON ASSOCIATION

Denison Parent-Teachers' Association will hold an all day quilting at the school Thursday, Feb. 7th.

DAWNING CLUB

Dawning Mothers' Club will meet Thursday, Feb. 14th, at Dawning School. Members are requested to bring carpet rags for the bazaar, which will be held in conjunction with an entertainment March 28th. All mothers who expect to attend the Congress of Mothers, at Hollenden Hotel, are asked to meet at Dawning School Monday, Feb. 4th, at 12:45. Donations for the bazaar are to be given to Mrs. Obarrath, on Cecelia ave.

B. H. PARENT-TEACHERS

Brooklyn Heights Parent-Teachers' Association will have an all day sewing meeting at the school, February 5. It has been asked that all members who can do so will bring sewing machines or motors. This association is also planning an oyster supper and dance for February 15. Mrs. Clyde Allen is chairman of the committee in charge. She is assisted by Mrs. Van Fleet.

BOWLING SCORES

After the bowling in the tournament in the Brooklyn Catholic Club last Wednesday evening, Al Miller and Tony Augustine held first place in the doubles by a score of 1207. They also equaled the high marks for doubles with a score of 402. Miller rolled 255 in a game Wednesday night and took Wednesday night's prize for the high score. Al Kopl is still leading the singles with a 703 mark and Walter Hahn is running second with 678.
While trying to thaw out a frozen radiator in the garage of E. Engler, Albert Kraft was overcome by gas. [text continues below column fold]

HEALING EVANGELISTS AT PRESBYTERIAN CHURCH
[photo] Rev. J. Lyle Shaw

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED
Why guess about the relative value of the advertising ability of the two Brooklyn newspapers when facts are conclusive and within the reach of all. Number of Advertisers for January, 1924 — The Brooklyn News ... 442; Brooklyn's other paper ... 185; Brooklyn News Supremacy ... 257. Greater distribution, coupled with the policy of the lowest possible advertising rate to all, contribute largely to the success of The Brooklyn News.

LUMBER CO. GIVES BOOK OF HOME PLANS FREE
A book of 50 practical and beautiful house plans and illustrations is being given away free by the Suburban Lumber Co., State and Brookpark roads, to the public.

REPORTS SHOW BUSINESS IS GOOD IN BROOKLYN
LODRICK'S BUSINESS GROWS

The W. J. Lodrick Motor Co., 4261 Pearl road, which opened up its business of used cars about a year ago, and has just recently built an office on the grounds, is now about to offer another service. This company is constructing its own garage to be used for a repair shop, where every car that is sold by this company will be reconditioned before being delivered to the purchaser. "The service we have always rendered our customers and the strict adherence to the fact that every buyer must be satisfied, is the secret of the success of this company," says Lodrick.

BROOKLYN COAL AND COKE CO. REPORTS BIG MONTH

Another report that business is good in Brooklyn comes from The Brooklyn Coal and Coke Co., 4107 Pearl Road, which announces that the January just past, was the biggest tonnage January in the company's history. W. B. McDiarmid, president, says that because of increasing business, the company intends in the near future to employ another responsible representative.

"BUSINESS IS GOOD," IS REPORT OF BATTERY MAN

"There is no such thing this year as business being poor during the month of January," says David Frey, president of the Southwest Battery Co., 4225 Pearl Road. According to his own statement, The Southwest Battery Co. had as much business during the first 18 days of January, as it generally has during the entire month. Frey says that they are prepared for even a larger volume of business, for they have just received an order of 68 Willard batteries for next month's demand.

BASKET BALL MANAGERS!

Managers of Brooklyn basket ball teams who desires to form a league at Glenn hall are asked to attend a meeting at the hall February 4, at 8 p. m.

YUM, YUM, YUM, JUICY ORANGES FOR NOTHING

If any Brooklyn family goes orangeless Saturday it will not be the fault of the Broadview Market, for the management will give a half dozen juicy, Sunkist navel oranges away absolutely free to every Brooklyn adult who calls for them between 7 a. m. and noon. There are no conditions of any kind, except that the coupon appearing in the Broadview Market Ad of this issue must be presented in order to obtain the oranges.

K. OF P'S PLAN TO ERECT NEW HOME
To Build On Organization's Broadview Road Site — Stores on First Floor

A new lodge home for South Brooklyn Lodge No. 426, K. of P., will soon become a reality if plans now under way mature successfully. The organization is planning to erect an attractive new building on its property on Broadview Road, east of Pearl Road. The lower floor will be constructed for store rooms and the second floor will be used for the lodge rooms. County Deputy G. C. J. Hall will make his annual official visit to the South Brooklyn lodge February 7. All members are urged to attend.

PLAN MEETING ON CHINA
Brooklyn Y. W. C. A. To Study Orient Feb. 7.

An evening devoted to China and the problems of Chinese women is being planned by Brooklyn Branch Y. W. C. A. The affair will be held at the Pearl Rd. M. E. Church, Feb. 7, at 8 o'clock. Mrs. Royce D. Fry will tell of her visit to Helen Rysdorp of the Cleveland Y. W. C. A. who for the past five years has been a missionary in China. Miss Hwang, a Chinese student from Ohio State University, will tell of the women and girls in China today. Chinese goods will be offered for sale in a booth in which Mrs. E. Konker and Mrs. Carl Webber will be in charge.

MISS DRAZIL DIES

Funeral services were held last Wednesday for Miss Rose Drazil, who died Sunday at the tuberculosis sanitarium. She was the daughter of Mrs. Anna Drazil, 4310 Muriel avenue. She was 21 years old and a graduate of Our Lady of Good Counsel school. Funeral services were conducted by the Rev. S. J. Kremer, pastor of Our Lady of Good Counsel Catholic church.

W. B. A. DANCE FEB. 9

The Guard of Riverside Review, No. 29, W. B. A. of Maccabees, will hold their annual dance Saturday evening, Feb. 9, in Herriman Hall, 3025 Vega Ave. Kasper's orchestra will furnish music. Small admission fee will be charged.

PLAYERS KEPT BUSY

The Geltman Orchestra, comprised of the three small talented children of Judge Herman Geltman of Parma, are much in demand as entertainers these days. Tonight (Friday) they will play at the Parma school entertainment. The boys are Bobbie, Marvin and Alvin, aged 3, 6 and 9.

OPENS CHIROPRACTIC OFFICE IN BROOKLYN

C. A. Hohler, chiropractor, has opened offices at 4402 Pearl Road. He is a graduate of Ross College of Chiropractic at Fort Wayne, Ind.

Y THEATER INSTALLS TWO NEW PROJECTORS

Two picture projection machines, that throw upon the screen clear, flickerless pictures and show perspective, have been installed by the Y Theater, State and W. 35th st. They are the first machines of their kind to be installed in any theater on the West Side, says Manager Sam Schachtel.

Y. M. C. A. NEWS
J. W. BUTTRISS

Church League Basketball — Pearl M. E. was the first team to defeat the Archwood seniors in the church league series. Trinity tackles Archwood next week. Schedule — Thursday, Feb. 7th: 7:30 Lincoln Srs. vs. Brooklyn Catholic Club; 8:15 Brooklyn M. E. vs. Pearl M. E.; 9:00 Trinity vs. Archwood. Indians Start a Band — Boys want to do something worth while, so they start a band.

GUESTS AT SHOWER AT MRS. M. F. CUTTING HOME

Mrs. Hazel De Pew and Mrs. Matilda Prahl were guests of honor at a stork shower Friday evening at the home of Mrs. Maggie Cutting, on Spring rd. Members of the Brooklyn Heights Sisterhood 245, Dames of Malta, were the guests. A color scheme of pink and white had been carried out in the dining room, where storks and dolls predominated as decorations. Following the supper the guests were entertained with games and music. Mrs. Cutting was assisted in entertaining by Mrs. J. C. Cowgill and Mrs. Hohr.

REBEKAHS PLAN SURPRISE FOR MEMBERS

Glendalia Rebekah Lodge is planning a surprise for its members at the regular meeting tonight (Friday). All members are asked to be present. A card party is being held by this order this afternoon at Glen Hall, Broadview and Pearl road.

PYTHIAN SISTERS INSPECTION

Brooklyn Temple Pythian Sisters had inspection January 22, when Grand Deputy Bessie Wittmore was presented with a beautiful silver basket. Lunch was served. Brooklyn Temple Pythian Sisters meets the second and fourth Tuesday of each month at Castle Hall, on Broadview Rd.
Clara Bradley, 718 L. A. to B. R. T., will have a card party Monday evening, February 4, at 8 p. m., at A. I. U. Hall, 4154 Pearl Rd. Lunch will be served.

MALTA DAMES PLAN CARD PARTY SERIES

Brooklyn Heights Sisterhood 245, Dames of Malta, are planning a series of evening card parties to provide funds for robes. The affairs are in charge of Mrs. Maggie Cutting, assisted by Mrs. F. Sands, Mrs. C. Shellac, Mrs. Helen Warner, Mrs. Z. Nicolaus, Mrs. Clara Quantz, Mrs. K. Simmons and Mrs. A. Cowgill.

F. O. HORN BUYS TIRE SHOP

Fred O. Horn, formerly 4158 Pearl road, who for five years has been in the moving, hauling and trucking business in Brooklyn, has just purchased the Davis Tire & Repair Shop, at 4132 Pearl road. Horn has purchased the entire interests and stock of the Davis Co., and along with conducting his newly purchased tire and repair shop, he will continue his moving and expressing.

CHURCH NEWS
EVANGELICAL ST. LUKE'S CHURCH — Memphis Ave. at Pearl Rd. F. H. Mittendorf, Pastor. English services next Sunday morning at 10:30. Sermon based on Matthew 8:25, "The Cry of the Perishing." Sunday School and Bible Class will meet at 9 a. m.
EIGHTH REFORMED CHURCH — W. 25th and Willowdale. Bible school 9:15 a. m. Morning service 10:45 a. m., sermon subject "Christian Youth."
SALEM METHODIST EPISCOPAL CHURCH — 4004 Cypress Ave. Wm. Jauch, Pastor.
PEARL ROAD METHODIST EPISCOPAL CHURCH — John H. Blackburn, D. D., Pastor.
STATE ROAD M. E. CHURCH — Glenn C. Cornell, Pastor.
THE PARMA CHURCH NEWS — Five new members united with the church Sunday.
BROOKLYN MEMORIAL M. E. CHURCH — Archwood and West 25th St. John W. Baxter, Pastor. Old Timers' Day, Sunday, Feb. 3, 1924.
UNITY EV. LUTHERAN CHURCH — R. G. Long, Pastor.

NEWS OF WOMAN'S CIVIC LEAGUE

Tuesday, Feb. 5th, the executive board will hold its regular meeting at the League House at 3:00 p. m. There will be a speaker on the subject of "Peace." Thursday, Feb. 7th, is the next program of the Cleveland Symphony Orchestra. Division of music of the Federation of Women's Clubs will meet in parlors D and E of Hotel Statler, Tuesday, Feb. 12, at 11 a. m. Feb. 21st will be the next monthly card party in charge of Mrs. E. Kenninger. Miss Amy Wolbach, of Easton, Pa., will open the dressmaking parlors at the Civic League House Monday, Feb. 4th.

LOESCH INSTALLS BALLOON TIRES

Orville Loesch, of the Loesch Tire & Repair Shop, 4262 Pearl road, has just put in a supply of balloon tires. "Many people have a lot of questions to ask about these new tires and I am prepared to answer them," says Loesch.

PYTHIAN SISTERS PARTY REPORTED SUCCESSFUL

Pythian Sisters 425 held a successful card party Tuesday evening. Among the prize winners were Mrs. Carrie Curtis, Mrs. Youngblood, Mrs. Shell, Mrs. Peble and Mrs. Meyers. The next card party will be held Tuesday evening, Feb. 19, at Castle Hall. The public is invited.
Ernest Engler, who has been conducting a tinshop at 4608 Spokane ave., has sold his property.

WILLIAM MORLOCK OVERCOME BY FUMES FROM AUTO

William Morlock, 3721 W. 25th St., was overcome by fumes from his automobile in his garage last Sunday. Captain Dryer and his crew from Engine House No. 24, was immediately summoned when Morlock was discovered, and rendered first aid.
The next regular meeting of the Brooklyn Heights Sisterhood 245, Dames of Malta, will be held February 11. There will be initiation at that time.
Mr. and Mrs. E. Collingwood have moved into a new home in Bungalow Gardens, at 1926 Creston ave.

WM. SCHROEDER KILLED

William Schroeder, 4256 W. 22nd st., died Monday, Jan. 28th, at Huron Road Hospital. He was injured last Monday at the Cleveland garbage plant, and died from injuries received. Funeral services were held last Thursday. Rev. Brandes, of St. Mark's Lutheran Church, officiated. Burial was made in Lutheran Cemetery. He is survived by his widow, Christena, and the following sons and daughters: Emily, Albert, William, Minnie, Anna, Charley, Henry, Elizabeth and Emma. He was 63 years of age.

MANY CROWD TO HEALING SERVICES
Evangelists In Brooklyn U. P. Church Attract People From All Parts Of City

People from all parts of Cleveland are helping to swell the crowds of South Brooklyn people who fill the auditorium of Brooklyn United Presbyterian Church, at Pearl and Spokane ave. They came to see the "Signs and Wonders," promised by J. Lyle Shaw and John W. Sproul, healing evangelists, and they were not disappointed. Many Brooklyn people who have been attending the meetings testified to cures and relief of various ailments. Their testimonies ranged from the discarding of crutches to the unexpected raising of money to pay off mortgages. According to the evangelist the cures are accomplished by faith. The evangelists conduct services every evening at 7:30 except Monday. The Shaw-Sproul evangelistic party will stay in Brooklyn a month.

OF INTEREST TO I. O. O. F.

The I. O. O. F. will give a grand ball at Hotel Cleveland, Oct. 20. All members of the Brooklyn Lodge are invited.

MANY HELP JAMES DAY CELEBRATE

A large gathering of friends and business associates attended the housewarming given by James Day in his new sign painting headquarters, 4099 Pearl road. The new quarters were fittingly decorated with signs. An informal reception was held during the afternoon and in the evening refreshments were served.

CHRYSLER SIXES ARE ATTRACTING ATTENTION

"The new Chrysler sixes are creating so much interest that 30-minute demonstrations are booked for two weeks in advance," says Floyd O. Holden, of the Holden Motor Sales Co., 4156 Pearl road. "These cars have literally taken the country by storm." R. R. Fitzwater, Holden sales manager, has the record of having delivered more cars than any associate dealer in the city during December. V. Wickliffe is the latest to join the Holden selling force. A. C. Dietze has recently joined the selling force of the Mellen D'Ewert Co., Brooklyn branch of Studebaker agency.

BOTH FATHER AND SON IN REALTY BUSINESS

"There is no better place in the county to buy a homesite than in the Brooklyn territory — that's why I am selling homesites in the community," says Robert Kennedy, Sr., of Bader ave. Both father and son are connected with the Brooklyn branch of the Findlay Co., marketers of Orchard Acres 1, 2, 3 and 4; Broadview Acres, and several other large parcels in the Brooklyn territory. Robert Kennedy, Sr., formerly was with the W. & L. E. Railroad for 24 years. The Brooklyn office of the Findlay Co. is located at 4152 Pearl rd.

"WHY WORRY" WITH LLOYD? — YOU CAN'T, IT'S TOO FUNNY

"How does the boy do it?" you hear in awesome and admiring tones from those who have watched the progress of Harold Lloyd during the last three years. Now we have "Why Worry" to not only laugh at, but to shake our heads at and marvel over. It is Lloyd's first serious attempt at straight farce. Conspicuous among Lloyd's aides in "Why Worry" are Jobyna Ralston and John Aasen. Aasen is an 8 foot 9 inch giant. "Why Worry" is a riot of fun, and the only thing for you to worry about is getting into the Y Theatre during its run next Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.

WHO IS BOK???

Who is this man Bok, anyway, that he thinks he knows how to draw up a peace plan? Would you believe that anyone would ask that question? It doesn't seem possible, but someone did. In fact, more than one person did and those who ask were intelligent people — leaders of thought in some directions. Yet the Bok peace plan has been discussed in newspapers and magazines for months. It has been discussed by churches, clubs and organizations of all kinds that are trying to make the world better. Maybe you will not believe in the Bok peace plan, but there are few normal people who do not believe in peace and welcome any move that will bring it nearer and nearer. At least do not condemn the plan unheard. Get a copy of it and read it. You can get a copy at the Brooklyn Y. M. C. A.

TO THE LIVING ABOUT THE DEAD

Three thousand years ago lived an Egyptian King named TUT-ANKH-AMEN. The name sounded like a stutter, so fellow Israelites called him "Tut" for short. When "Tut" reached the DANGEROUS AGE and finally succeeded in producing the "Staycomb" effect with his somewhat luxuriant locks, he up and died. They proceeded to wrap him up, per custom, in a series of layers and finally deposited the remains in a tomb in the Valley of Departed Kings. Three thousand years later, a party of scribes, while exploring, dug up "Tut's" tomb with all the medieval relics buried with him. Then the advertising men stepped in and took charge, and in a few weeks gave "Tut" a reputation which shades CHARLIE CHAPLIN, DOUG. FAIRBANKS and MARY PICKFORD into oblivion by comparison. Moral: You might have the best product in the world, but unless you TELL them about it, your business will slumber peacefully to death. And that is why I advertise to you folks in the Brooklyn-Parma community. I want you to know that I have a science that REALLY and ACTUALLY ADJUSTS the CAUSES of one's troubles. I practice the most nearly perfect cure in the world for all disease. — C. A. Hohler, D. C., Chiropractor, 4402 Pearl Road.
